subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift guards as a core durable run-state contract, and what artifact, timer, persistence, and flag semantics should that contract enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix chooses public runtime semantics, persisted state ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and config or feature-flag shape across core agent execution.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle Work
options.body: Make these acceptance criteria part of the broader atomic begin/exec/commit-or-abort lifecycle design so OpenClaw has one progress-state source of truth.

options.title: Keep Adjacent Safeguards Only
options.body: Treat current loop, liveness, and no-fake-progress mitigations as sufficient and narrow or close this issue after explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, no-idle-after-green behavior, persistence, and compatibility before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice defines core runtime/product semantics and steipete is the code-owner and strongest recent adjacent product-contract reviewer in the inspected history.
